section_summary.extract_value: This Measures section describes the questionnaires used in the present study, including a Demographic Questionnaire (height and weight collected to compute BMI), the Body Appreciation Scale (BAS), two MBSRQ subscales (Appearance Evaluation and Body Areas Satisfaction), and sexual function/distress/satisfaction measures (FSFI, FSDS, NSSS). The section reports some sample-level results (e.g., four women not sexually active, 35.8% below FSFI cutoff, 34% with clinically significant sexual distress) but does not provide overall sample size, country, recruitment/source details, survey administration method, or correlations between BAS and BMI.
section_summary.evidence_source: This measure was used to gather information on personal (e.g., age, level of education, ethnicity) and relationship demographics (e.g., relationship status, relationship duration). Information on height and weight was collected in order to calculate the participants' BMI. Body Appreciation Scale (BAS; Avalos et al., 2005) This self-report questionnaire evaluates the extent to which individuals hold favorable opinions and respect toward their body. Overall, four women reported that they had not been sexually active in the past four weeks. In addition, 35.8% of the total sample reported a total score below the cutoff, thus suggesting clinically significant sexual dysfunction. In the present sample, 34% of participants reported a clinically significant level of sexual distress.
